headline: Methods for single-cell perturbation, regulatory networks and spatial decontamination
label: Single Cell Multiomic Profiling
summary: Recent benchmarks show that method choice drives in silico perturbation results, prompting closer scrutiny of single-cell inference tools.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is methodological scrutiny of single-cell and spatial transcriptomic inference. Several items propose or benchmark tools for in silico perturbation. One systematic evaluation of eight methods reports that six fail to detect TF-to-pathway signals, and a mechanism-annotated benchmark finds that expression similarity poorly reflects drug-response mechanism. Other items address spatial decontamination of RNA leakage and mRNA lateral diffusion, causal gene regulatory network inference from scRNA-seq, reference-free identification of cell states and markers, and sparse classification of disease from patient-level pseudobulk profiles. The newest element is a shift toward evaluation rigor, in which predicted perturbation and network outputs are tested against mechanism rather than accepted on expression similarity. The items vary in maturity, and most are unreviewed preprints.
